name: Carbetocin

overview.mechanism: Uterotonic activity is used to prevent postpartum blood loss; the cited trials concern administration after birth, not labor induction [[CARB-CHAMP]].
uses: Prevention of postpartum hemorrhage studied after vaginal birth and cesarean delivery; verify the approved formulation, route and indication locally [[CARB-CHAMP,CARB-HEMO]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Double-blind noninferiority trial; 29,645 women; 23 sites in 10 countries.
rows.intervention: Heat-stable carbetocin versus oxytocin immediately after vaginal birth.
rows.findings: Blood loss ≥500 mL or additional uterotonic use occurred in 14.5% versus 14.4% (RR 1.01; 95% CI 0.95–1.06), meeting noninferiority. For blood loss ≥1,000 mL, noninferiority was not established.
rows.limitations: Low frequency of the ≥1,000-mL outcome limited power. Prevention after vaginal birth does not establish treatment of ongoing hemorrhage or justify substituting formulations/routes.

rows.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 76 elective cesarean deliveries under spinal anesthesia.
rows.intervention: Carbetocin, oxytocin or placebo after delivery.
rows.findings: Carbetocin and oxytocin had comparable hemodynamic effects; mean systolic pressure fell by 26 and 28 mmHg, respectively.
rows.limitations: Small perioperative trial; no renal-impairment regimen or long-term cardiovascular safety established.

sources.citation: Heat-Stable Carbetocin versus Oxytocin to Prevent Hemorrhage after Vaginal Birth. PubMed PMID: 29949473.
Changes in blood pressure and cardiac output during cesarean delivery: the effects of oxytocin and carbetocin compared with placebo. PubMed PMID: 23598289.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

serious: Acute hypotension occurred in the perioperative hemodynamic trial; comparable effects to oxytocin do not mean no cardiovascular risk [[CARB-HEMO]].

renal: The cited obstetric trials do not establish an advanced-CKD or dialysis regimen. Product-specific renal restrictions must be checked rather than inferred from prevention efficacy [[CARB-CHAMP,CARB-HEMO]].
